title: A Polynomial-Scaling PDE Solver with Entanglement-Basis Tensor Networks
authors: Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Michael J. Landry, Chu-Liang Fu, Mingda Li
abstract: We develop a finite element method (FEM) for partial differential equation (PDE) solver based on the entanglement-basis representation introduced in our companion work. By lifting non-linear finite-element equations into an augmented coefficient space, the governing PDE together with boundary, initial, and inter-element constraints can be expressed through a unified quadratic residual minimization. Although this augmented space grows exponentially with the number of elements, its tensor-product structure allows it to be represented efficiently using tensor networks. Using the matrix product state (MPS) as a concrete example, we show that density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) sweeps enable element-by-element optimization without explicitly constructing the full augmented space. For bounded bond dimension, the resulting computational cost scales polynomially with the number of finite elements. We extend the framework to time-dependent problems through implicit temporal discretization and demonstrate convergence under both mesh and polynomial refinement using diffusion equations.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Tensor Network Finite Element (TN-FE) method to solve PDEs with polynomial scaling. It reformulates the PDE residual minimization into a tensor network structure, allowing the use of efficient algorithms like DMRG sweeps. This makes solving large, complex PDEs tractable by exploiting the assumed locality of correlations in the underlying physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a computationally efficient solver for Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) that overcomes the exponential scaling inherent in traditional methods.
main_result: They achieve polynomial scaling in the number of finite elements by representing the PDE residual minimization problem within a Tensor Network (TN) framework.
method: The core method combines the Finite Element Method (FEM) with Tensor Networks (TNs), mapping the PDE residual into a TN structure and using DMRG sweeps for efficient, element-by-element optimization.
model_or_system: The framework is general, applicable to analytic operator equations (OEs) and demonstrated on a 1D diffusion equation. It handles general PDEs by reducing them to OEs.
key_observables: The weighted residual norm J(c), the solution u(x, t), and the convergence of the solution with respect to basis order and element count.
important_parameters: The computational cost scales polynomially with the number of elements, controlled by the bond dimension (S) and correlation order.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the underlying physics admits a compact Tensor Network representation, implying a locality of correlation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the TN representation of the residual term, the choice of TN ansatzes (MPS, PEPS), and the convergence of the solver for the diffusion equation compared to standard methods.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general mathematical formulation of PDEs as OEs, introduces the TN-FE framework for residual minimization, details the implementation of building block operators (derivatives, multiplication), and finally demonstrates convergence using a time-dependent diffusion equation example.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, scalable numerical tool for simulating complex quantum or condensed matter dynamics described by PDEs, directly bridging quantum many-body simulation techniques (TNs) with continuum physics (PDEs).
